 Tata Power Q2 review: Brokerages remain bullish on renewables and Mundra resolution
 Elevated fuel expenses weighed on operating margins in Q2, but brokerages see growth visibility from renewable capacity additions, solar manufacturing and a potential resolution of the Mundra tariff issue. 
 Ritik Raj 
 ETEnergyWorld 
 Published On Nov 12, 2026 at 11:20 AM IST

 Image for representative purposes only. Tata Power Company Ltd delivered a steady second-quarter performance for FY27, though elevated fuel expenses weighed on its operating margins.
Reviewing the quarterly show, JM Financial pointed to a margin miss offset by renewable energy (RE) additions and visibility into the resolution of Mundra . In contrast, Elara Securities said strong triggers are ahead following an in-line operational performance.
 Renewable expansion 
RE and solar manufacturing remained the primary growth engines during the quarter. JM Financial highlighted that Tata Power commissioned 419 MW of utility-scale capacity in the second quarter, bringing total utility-scale capacity to 7.2 GW, while rooftop solar revenue grew 20 per cent YoY to ₹1,350 crore after adding 426 MW.
 Advt 
 Elara noted that an under-construction pipeline of 4.9 GW in renewables and 696 MWh in battery storage is providing strong medium-term growth visibility, supported by quarterly solar module output stabilising at 1 GW with a 97 per cent yield.
 Still, JM Financial noted that management's guidance to add 2.5 GW of renewable capacity in FY27 is an ambitious target the brokerage finds challenging.
On capital expenditure , the company invested ₹10,000 crore in the first half against an FY27 target of ₹25,000 crore, approved a 1,800 MW pumped hydro storage project at Shirawta with a ₹12,000 crore outlay, and plans ₹1,25,000 crore in capex over FY26–30 to achieve 20 GW of green capacity by FY30.
 Mundra outlook and regulatory progress 
At the 4,150 MW Mundra thermal plant, availability stood at 89 per cent under the extended Section 11 mandate, which runs through December 31, 2026.
JM Financial said "hope alive for Mundra" as a regulatory tariff order for its supplemental power purchase agreement with Gujarat is expected before year-end, which should prompt other states to sign similar pacts.
 Meanwhile, Odisha distribution companies lowered aggregate technical and commercial losses to 21 per cent. Both brokerages also tracked the Singapore arbitration dispute with Kleros Capital, where an appeal hearing is slated for January 19, 2027, and management expects a favourable resolution in 6-8 months.
 Advt 
 Projections and ratings 
For the upcoming fiscal years, JM Financial expects net sales to rise 16.6 per cent to ₹74,246.2 crore in FY27 and ₹82,544.5 crore in FY28, with adjusted net profit reaching ₹4,964.1 crore and ₹5,407.1 crore, respectively.
 Elara Securities projects FY27 revenue at ₹73,049.7 crore and net profit at ₹6,496.4 crore.
Accounting for a potential ₹6,113 crore arbitration liability, Elara Securities retained its ‘Buy’ rating on Tata Power but trimmed its target price to ₹485 from ₹504.
JM Financial maintained its ‘Buy’ rating and raised its target price to ₹419 from ₹406, citing momentum in renewables and visibility into the Mundra resolution .
